reading.thesis: Sisay is a mana-to-battlefield converter whose exchange rate is her own power: five coloured pips buy one legendary permanent, every new colour she buys widens the next purchase, and the currency every other stage is paying for is ACCESS rather than cards or mana.

lines.name: ignition → conversion
lines.note: Each of these puts two colours on the battlefield for two mana, and the fetch pool goes 3 -> 10 -> 23 targets at 0, 1 and 2 colours among other legends. This is the arrow the deck's opening hand is really about.

lines.name: fuel → conversion
lines.note: The tutor finds permanents in the library; it cannot find the 26 nonland non-legendary cards, and it never puts a card in your hand. These three do. Reki is the qualified one: it triggers on CASTING a legendary spell, and Sisay's ability does not cast.

lines.name: conversion → fuel
lines.note: The interlock the ladder hides. Esika and Selvala are mana value 3, legal at power 4 — two other colours — and are the fetches that actually change your mana. Jegantha is mana value 5, legal only at power 6, so the one card that solves the colour problem outright is the last one she can reach. Fetch mana early or draw it.
v1_via: Esika, God of the Tree // The Prismatic Bridge

lines.name: conversion → output
lines.note: What the ladder is for: one tax permanent blanks plans at three seats, and each one fetched is also another colour, which widens the next fetch. The rungs and the payoffs are the same cards.

lines.name: fuel → wincon
lines.note: Verified: Derevi's untap triggers equal the attacker count while Najeela's cost stays fixed at five, so combat 2 is exactly break-even (5 triggers, 5 mana) and combat 3 onward is surplus. The loop is unbounded and it is not self-contained.

open_questions.question: Re-run stack 001 (Sisay activated the turn she lands, and the escalating fetch chain) with the single -X/-X clause the checker flagged. Does the deck's central line — pay five pips, fetch a legend, recalculate power mid-resolution, fetch again — pass?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Every arrow leaving `conversion` is currently dashed and the columnists are barred from asserting a dashed line. The checker's own note says answers (a) through (e) were independently verified correct and only the iteration bound stopped it, so the deck's defining interaction is one clause away from being the fact this model most needs.

open_questions.question: Re-run stack 003 (Relic of Legends versus Esika's granted ability on a legend Sisay put onto the battlefield this turn), fixing the step-13 Esika vigilance attribution and the step-14 ceiling the checker refuted. Can a freshly fetched legend help pay for the NEXT activation, and what is the real per-turn mana ceiling?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the difference between one activation a turn and two. If a fetched body can be tapped for mana the same turn through Relic's non-{T} cost while Esika's granted {T} ability is locked out by summoning sickness, the ladder can climb twice, and the `fuel -> conversion` arrow becomes the deck's real engine rather than a claim.

open_questions.question: Add a win-line target and measure it: how often are Najeela plus a mana base that can produce all five colours both available, and by which turn?
open_questions.why_it_matters: goldfish_targets declares four targets and not one measures a win line, so the deck's only rules-verified kill has never been priced. findings.claim: Jodah's cast cost is five pips, "a bill The Prismatic Bridge — Esika's back face, {1}{G}{G} in hand under CR 712.4a and {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} if you cast that side — also pays"
findings.note: The SUBSTANCE of the repair is right and is the correct rebuttal to round 2: card_faces in cards.json give Esika, God of the Tree {1}{G}{G} and The Prismatic Bridge {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}, so the uniqueness superlative is properly withdrawn rather than rephrased, and the tie ('Surrak and Kenrith tie him' at mana value 5, legal only at power 6) recomputes exactly — max cmc in the whole 99 is 5.0. The RULE NUMBER is wrong. Against the rules DB this repo builds (CR 2026-06-19), 712.4a reads 'One card in each meld pair has an ability that exiles both that object and its counterpart and melds them' — it is the MELD rule and says nothing about modal double-faced cards. The rule the sentence needs is 712.8a: 'While a double-faced card is outside the game or in a zone other than the battlefield or stack, it has only the characteristics of its front face.' Refutable in one command: `manamap pilot lookup-rule 712.4a`. PARTIALLY MECHANICALLY CHECKABLE, and the gap is instructive: an id-existence check passes here, because 712.4a exists and is simply about something else. The check that would catch it is the one validate_stack already enforces on stacks — a CR id in engine prose must carry a verbatim quote from that rule.

findings.claim: "Emiel does not untap: he blinks, and the returned body is summoning-sick, so it turns a source over only under Samut's haste."
findings.note: The repair's first half is correct and was the right call — Emiel's oracle is '{3}: Exile another target creature you control, then return it to the battlefield', the returned permanent is a new object, and CR 302.6 bars its own {T} ability that turn; Samut, Voice of Dissent's 'Other creatures you control have haste' lifts exactly that bar. The word 'only' does not survive the stage's own card list. Relic of Legends, a member of this stage's declared six-card component, reads 'Tap an untapped legendary creature you control: Add one mana of any color' — the tap is a COST paid by the Relic's ability, not the creature's own {T} symbol, so CR 302.6 does not apply and a summoning-sick body can pay it. Blink Selvala, Esika or Jegantha with Emiel and each returns untapped and taps to Relic for a mana with no haste anywhere. Either the 'only' is false, or the Relic route is unsettled — and the model itself says it is unsettled, in open_questions[1], which is built on 'Relic's non-{T} cost' on a freshly arrived legend. A settled negative cannot be asserted about a question the same artifact files as open. Cheapest honest fixes: delete the Emiel sentence (evidence[2] already files him as a candidate combo line, not a fact), or write 'only under Samut's haste or as Relic of Legends' tap cost'.

findings.claim: "The untap half — Ioreth, Samut, Emiel, Derevi, Seedborn Muse — turns those sources over again"
findings.note: Emiel the Blessed does not untap anything. v1_stages.label: THE FIVE-PIP BILL
v1_stages.what_it_does: The activation this deck exists to make costs {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} — five coloured pips with zero generic — so none of the deck's generic acceleration touches it. That is why 39 land entries carry the load and only four rocks come along. Black is the ceiling: mana_analysis reports W 26, G 27, U 22, R 21 and B 21 sources, against a Karsten target of 36 for black (Sheoldred is {2}{B}{B}) and 22 for the other four; on-curve probability for black is 0.299 on lands alone and 0.610 once rocks and dorks are counted, against 0.944 W and 0.951 G. Black carries 11.1% of the pip load and 18.5% of the sources, so the shortfall is not about casting Toxic Deluge on time — it is that the activation you want to make every turn is one black source away from not happening. The declared 'Early accelerant drawn' component is seven cards: 41.2% in the opener, 49.8% by turn three, 74.7% assembled, mean turn 2.836. Plaza of Heroes sits here because stack 002 taps and untaps it for four of the five pips, though mana_analysis credits it with zero colour sources: both coloured modes are conditional. It is NOT tutorable: its type line is Land, Sisay searches for a legendary permanent card, and no fetchland here finds it either — so its hexproof-and-indestructible mode is protection she can never reach. Delighted Halfling pays none of them: its any-colour mana is spend-only-to-cast-a-legendary-spell and these five pips are an ACTIVATION cost, so mana_analysis records it as producing nothing. Birds of Paradise, unrestricted, pays exactly one of the five. Mox Amber is here rather than at ignition because it is colourless: one of only three legendary permanents below mana value 2, it adds nothing to Sisay's power and produces nothing until a legendary creature or planeswalker is on the board.

v1_stages.label: THE SECOND COLOUR
v1_stages.what_it_does: Nothing in this deck happens on schedule until Sisay's ability reaches more than three cards, and what it reaches is set by the number of colours among OTHER legendary permanents you control. Counted over cards.json: 3 / 10 / 23 / 28 / 33 / 33 targets at 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 colours. The number to hold is TWO, where access more than doubles. These six are the cheapest way there — coloured legendary permanents at mana value 2 or less whose job is not the dial and not a shield, four of them carrying two colours on one card. They share no text at all: Kinnan doubles nonland mana, Lotho taxes second spells into Treasure, Rona loots and untaps on legendary casts, Saffi buys a creature back, Katilda gives Humans (Sisay included) a mana ability, Yoshimaru just grows itself. In this engine their first job is identical — be a coloured legendary permanent on turn two, so the first activation is not choosing between Mox Amber, Yoshimaru and Mikaeus. Sisay herself is filed at conversion, not here: she is the machine rather than the starting gun, and what has to be true before her first activation is worth making is a board state, not a card. Nothing in goldfish_targets measures this, which is the gap the frame's own reading points at — 'Sisay plus payoffs is a hand of payoffs'.

v1_stages.label: PAYING FOR THE SECOND ACTIVATION
v1_stages.what_it_does: One activation per turn cycle is value; two is something else, and this stage buys the extras. The six declared multi-colour mana sources are not interchangeable. Only Jegantha adds all five off one tap, and its can't-pay-generic clause is irrelevant against a cost with no generic. Bloom Tender and Faeburrow Elder pay one mana per colour among ALL permanents you control — not the number printed on Sisay, which counts colours among OTHER LEGENDARY permanents. Ten nonlegendary coloured permanents in this 99 — including both Vivid dorks counting themselves — move the Vivid count, not the dial. Vivid is a superset: never behind the ladder, usually ahead. Esika grants every OTHER legendary creature '{T}: Add one mana of any color', turning each fetched body into a source. Selvala adds X in any combination for your greatest creature power, often Sisay. Relic of Legends, the sixth, taps a legendary creature as a COST, not that creature's own {T}. Measured: 36.4% in the opener, assembled 67.9%, 55.8% by turn 6, mean turn 4.219, six cards deep. The untap half — Ioreth, Samut, Derevi, Seedborn Muse — turns those sources over again, and only Derevi's is proved by a passing stack. Emiel does not untap: he blinks, and the returned body is summoning-sick, so its own {T} waits on Samut's haste — Relic's cost does not. The draw half (Rhystic Study, Esper Sentinel, Reki) refills a hand the tutor cannot reach: Sisay PUTS permanents onto the battlefield rather than casting them, so Reki does not trigger off her ability. This deck has no `fodder` stage: nothing is sacrificed, discarded or exiled as a cost to run the engine. Mikaeus converts one board resource into another, a counter off himself onto the team, but nothing consumes a resource to power it.
cards: Esika, God of the Tree // The Prismatic Bridge

v1_stages.label: THE DIAL
v1_stages.what_it_does: Sisay's gate reads POWER: 'search your library for a legendary permanent card with mana value less than Sisay's power'. Base 2/2, +1/+1 for each colour among other legendary permanents. Two routes move that number and the card does not care which produced it. Colour breadth: Dihada (three colours), Surrak (three), Jodah (five; his own cast cost is the same five pips, a bill The Prismatic Bridge — Esika's back face, {1}{G}{G} in hand under CR 712.8a and {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} if you cast that side — also pays; at mana value 5 he is legal only at power 6, and Surrak and Kenrith tie him there). Counters and anthems: Mikaeus taps to grow himself and then to grow the team, Bristly Bill puts a counter on every landfall, Heliod turns lifegain into counters, Kenrith buys counters and haste with spare mana, and Flowering of the White Tree gives legendary creatures +2/+1 permanently — two more mana value of reach, plus ward {1}. The declared 'three-colour legend to grow her' component is the thinnest in the deck: four cards, 25.8% in the opener, 41.9% by turn 6, assembled 52.5%. Where the ladder tops out is a fact about this 99 and not about the card — nothing here exceeds mana value 5, so power 6 buys everything and further power buys nothing. Sisay is the single point of failure for the entire model: she is the only card that converts mana into board, and losing her resets the recast tax and every rung already climbed. Her central line is NOT verified. Stack 001 walked exactly this chain and the checker exhausted its iteration bound on one clause, so every arrow leaving this stage is dashed.

v1_stages.label: WHAT ACCESS BUYS
v1_stages.what_it_does: Instead of ten removal spells the deck buys virtual advantage, and most of it sits on the battlefield where the tutor can reach it. Kutzil stops opponents casting during your turn; Teferi holds them to sorcery speed; Drannith Magistrate cuts them off from anywhere but hand; Thalia makes their creatures and nonbasic lands enter tapped; Kambal and Sheoldred convert their spells and their draws into loss; Dauthi Voidwalker exiles what would reach their graveyards. Loran and Path to Exile are the two targeted answers, Toxic Deluge the reset, Kodama the trample that makes a counter-laden board connect, and Raff the flash grant that lets you deploy legends with counterspell mana still up. The frame's reading of the tax shell holds: 'All six are legendary at mana value 2-4, so each sits inside the fetch pool from the second colour onward' — for those six the answer suite and the ladder's rungs are the same cards, which is exactly why access compounds rather than merely accumulates. It does not generalise to the stage: four of these twelve sit outside the fetch pool at any power, because Sisay searches for a legendary permanent card. Drannith Magistrate and Dauthi Voidwalker are nonlegendary creatures, Path to Exile is an instant and Toxic Deluge a sorcery; all four have to be drawn. deck-audit reads interaction at 8 copies (at target) and interaction-breadth at 3 of 5 classes. This is the one stage where the deck's own map agrees with the engine completely: all twelve sit in THE TOOLBOX, whose gloss — 'one answer at a time, chosen after you see the problem' — is a fair description of what a tutor is for.

v1_stages.label: INSURANCE ON THE ONLY ENGINE
v1_stages.what_it_does: The declared component is eleven cards and it is the healthiest thing in the deck: 57.4% in the opener, 67.0% by turn three, 88.4% assembled, 79.8% by turn 6, mean turn 2.3. All three of Cullen's classes are present — a constant that is itself tutorable (Shalai grants you and your other creatures hexproof), free or cheap instants (Fierce Guardianship, Flawless Maneuver, Heroic Intervention), and a denial layer (Grand Abolisher, Silence, Swan Song, An Offer You Can't Refuse, Dispel, Negate, Arcane Denial), plus Boros Charm's indestructible mode against a wrath. The structural fact the map states by accident: not one of the five cards in THE HELD ANSWERS is legendary, and neither are Heroic Intervention, Flawless Maneuver, Silence, Grand Abolisher or Boros Charm. The commander cannot fetch her own insurance. That is the frame's blind spot made concrete — 26 of the 99 are nonland and not legendary, and that set holds every instant in the deck and all four Game Changers. Protection here is a DRAW problem rather than an access problem, which is the opposite of every other stage in this model. Why the recast tax bites harder than usual: losing Sisay costs {2} more per prior command-zone cast AND every accumulated rung of access, so the protection is not insuring a body, it is insuring a position.

v1_stages.label: ONE CARD, AND THE ONLY VERIFIED THING HERE
v1_stages.what_it_does: Najeela. Stack 002 is this deck's only checker-passed artifact and it settles what the pair IS rather than anything about the bracket: with Derevi it is a deterministic, unbounded combat loop but NOT a self-contained two-card infinite. The floor does not rest on it — bracket_report reaches 4 twice over without Derevi, once from four Game Changers alone and once from a two-card-infinite driver listing four lines, three of which pair Najeela with Faeburrow Elder, Esika or Selvala. It produces no mana, so every iteration re-buys {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} from outside, and it needs at least five of your creatures connecting with a player. The arithmetic it establishes: attackers follow A' = 2A - 1 (3, 5, 9, 17, 33) and Derevi's untap triggers equal the attacker count while the cost stays fixed at five, so combat 1 is funded from pre-combat lands, COMBAT 2 IS BREAK-EVEN (5 triggers against 5 mana) and combat 3 onward runs a surplus. Damage per combat is A + 3 (6, 8, 12, 20, 36); the first opponent dies during combat 4, the second by combat 6, and the life cost floors at 0 per combat. The number to hold in your head is the break-even combat, not the card count. What this model will not claim is that the deck reliably arrives here: goldfish_targets declares four targets and not one of them measures a win line, so how often Najeela and a live five-colour base show up together has never been measured. deck-audit's threat-density counts Boros Charm, Kambal and Samut and not Najeela, so the taxonomy and this engine disagree about what a finisher is here. Everything else that could end a game is filed where its first job is — a board of legends under Jodah's anthem, with Kodama's trample and Kenrith's haste.

v1_map_disagreements.component: IGNITION — the second colour (six coloured legendary permanents at mana value 2 or less)
v1_map_disagreements.why: Three, two and one. These six share no text: a mana doubler, a Treasure tax, a looter, a recursion trick, a Human mana-granter and a dog that grows itself. The map files each under what it says, and none of them says the thing that matters — that it is a coloured legendary permanent castable on turn two. The property is printed on Sisay, not on them, so the map cannot see the class at all. This is the same law radagast's scatter demonstrated: a component is coherent on the map exactly when its defining property is printed on its members.

v1_map_disagreements.component: CONVERSION — the dial (Sisay plus the eight cards that move her power)
v1_map_disagreements.why: Four and five, and the split is not arbitrary — it is the two ROUTES to one number. Colour breadth (Dihada, Jodah, Surrak) reads as 'legendary permanents' and lands in THE TOOLBOX; counters and anthems (Mikaeus, Bristly Bill, Heliod, Kenrith, Flowering of the White Tree) read as 'counters' and land in GROW HER, GUARD HER. Sisay's gate reads POWER and does not care which route produced it, so the engine sees one stage where the map sees two.

5 / 3 / 3 in the scatter table. The map separates instants you HOLD from permanents that shield and from the tax bodies, which is a true distinction about text and the wrong one for the pilot: all of them are bought with the same held mana and compete for the same slot. The useful cut is orthogonal to all three cities — legendary versus not. Nothing in THE HELD ANSWERS is legendary, so the commander cannot fetch any of it.

v1_map_disagreements.component: Sisay online with a multi-colour mana engine (the declared 6-card component)
v1_map_disagreements.why: 5 / 1. Relic of Legends is an artifact, so it files with Sol Ring and Arcane Signet, and the picture then says it is an accelerant like they are. Functionally it is a legendary-creature tapper, which is what the artifact shelf hides: it taps a legendary creature as a COST, not that creature's own {T}, so it is not Esika — Esika is a legendary creature that GRANTS each other legendary creature a {T} ability of its own — and it is one of the three members of this component that are NOT legendary and can therefore never be fetched at any power.

v1_map_disagreements.component: MANA — Birds of Paradise and Delighted Halfling
v1_map_disagreements.why: The map puts both in MANA ON LEGS beside Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder and Jegantha, because all five are bodies that make coloured mana. The engine separates them, and for two different reasons. Birds of Paradise adds one unrestricted mana of any colour: it CAN pay a pip, and one of five is not an activation. Delighted Halfling cannot pay one at all — its any-colour mode reads 'spend this mana only to cast a legendary spell' and Sisay's and Najeela's costs are activations, not casts, so its only usable mana here is {C}. mana_analysis records exactly that split: Birds produces W/U/B/R/G and the Halfling produces nothing. The Vivid pair and Jegantha pay for the activation itself. One pip versus five is the difference between the mana stage and the fuel stage in this deck.
